subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should memory-lancedb expose a model-visible exact deletion selector from `memory_recall` now, or should this wait for the broader memory lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42650?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent contract has product implications: raw UUID exposure, opaque handles, numeric indices with transient state, or non-destructive replacement/deprecation all create different memory safety and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Expose recall deletion selectors now
options.body: Add a narrow model-visible UUID or opaque handle in `memory_recall` content so agents can pass it to `memory_forget(memoryId=...)`, and defer replacement/deprecation semantics to the Memory MVP tracker.

options.title: Design lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open as evidence under the broader memory review/edit/forget/conflict design and avoid a narrow selector change until tombstone/supersede semantics are settled.

options.title: Document current limitation only
options.body: Clarify that recall numbers are display indices and users must use `memory_forget(query=...)` or CLI listing for IDs, accepting that the reporter's direct handoff remains missing.

recommendation.title: Expose recall deletion selectors now
recommendation.body: Add a narrow model-visible UUID or opaque handle in `memory_recall` content so agents can pass it to `memory_forget(memoryId=...)`, and defer replacement/deprecation semantics to the Memory MVP tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-lancedb maintenance and the prior merged full-UUID candidate-list fix make this the best available routing candidate for deciding the narrow selector contract.
